Renault Taps GM's Diernaz as New Branding Chief
Renault named a new group chief branding officer, poaching a General Motors executive after former branding chief Arnaud Belloni left for Jeep maker Stellantis.

The French automaker said Jean-Pierre Diernaz will become vice president for Renault brand global marketing, as well as branding head for the group's other brands, Alpine and Dacia. Diernaz was until last month managing director and chief marketing officer for General Motors Europe, and previously held European positions at Ford and Japan's Nissan.

Diernaz's appointment, effective next week, comes after rival auto group Stellantis, maker of auto brands including Jeep, last month named Renault's Belloni as European marketing chief and chief executive of brands including Fiat.

Diernaz joins Renault at a time when it is seeking to sustain a rebound from a tough period of pressured sales and squeezed margins. The appointment comes at a "pivotal time" for the group, said Fabrice Cambolive, the company's chief growth officer and CEO of Renault brand.

"Over the past few years, we have embarked on a profound transformation, and our ambition is now to go even further-- harnessing the power of the brand, customer insights and new technologies to deliver stronger and more sustainable growth," Cambolive said.
